column4: Visit note | 2025-10-28 04:30 PM | Dr. Jannatul Ferdous, Orthopedics | Patient: Tamanna Khatun, 48, female. Mrs. Khatun reports having a stiff shoulder for weeks, making her unable to reach behind her back. She states that the pain and stiffness began after a minor fall at home in Tongi. She works as a security guard. She has Type 2 diabetes mellitus. She denies any previous neck injury, numbness down the arm, or skin discoloration over the joint. On examination: shoulder lifts only to 60 degrees, BP 114/78 mmHg, pulse 75 bpm, weight 68 kg. Passive rotation is severely restricted in all directions with pain at the end range. Assessment: Adhesive capsulitis. Plan: a prescription was issued. She was advised to start physiotherapy, do pendulum exercises daily, and apply heat before exercise. Follow-up in 4 weeks with a physiotherapy review.

Visit note | 2025-10-29 10:00 AM | Dr. Zahid Hasan, Gastroenterology | Patient: Khadija Awal, 74, female. Mrs. Awal describes a gnawing pain in her upper belly that often wakes her up at night. She mentions the trouble started after weeks of taking painkillers for back pain in Banani. She is a retired civil servant. She has Type 2 diabetes mellitus. She denies vomiting blood, black tarry stools, or unintended weight loss. On examination: pain score 7/10 on abdominal palpation in the epigastric region, BP 119/71 mmHg, pulse 76 bpm, weight 67 kg. Bowel sounds are normal and there is no abdominal rigidity. Assessment: Peptic ulcer disease. Plan: a prescription was issued. She was advised to avoid painkillers such as ibuprofen, stop smoking, and eat regular meals. Follow-up in 4 weeks with a stool H. pylori test.

Visit note | 2025-10-29 12:00 PM | Dr. Shamima Nasrin, Ophthalmology | Patient: Rahim Akand, 48, male. Mr. Akand attends for review regarding his gritty burning eyes, noting that his symptoms feel worse in air conditioning and that his eyes water all day rather than feeling dry. He works as an NGO field officer and mentions the irritation became worse since night shifts at a call centre in Shyamoli. He has Hypothyroidism. He denies double vision, severe eye pain, or flashes of light. On examination: tear break-up time 3 seconds, BP 136/70 mmHg, pulse 91 bpm, weight 93 kg. Corneas are clear with mild conjunctival injection bilaterally. Assessment: Dry eye syndrome. Plan: a prescription was issued. He was advised to look away from the screen every 20 minutes, blink often, and use a humidifier. Follow-up in 1 month.
